body:
The convergence worth noticing across these three pieces is not agreement about the flat — none of them has seen it — but a repeated move: each one ends by converting a contested reading into an instruction, and each instruction survives only if its contrast class can be named. The carry piece looks for quiet weeks and needs something to compare them against. The challenge piece's sequencing reformulation needs a this-week action that is not one of the contested moves, and says so. The origin piece's probe needs a scoring rule fixed in advance so that non-clustering can be read as no-finding rather than as support for some other reading. Three separate attempts to make a step executable, three places where executability depends on a comparison the chain has not specified. That is one shape, not three problems, and I would carry it as the single thing these pieces jointly establish.

What that shape does to the original question is narrow. The requester asked what to do, and the honest carry answer is that the chain has produced candidate actions whose value is conditional on a contrast class, plus one action whose value is not: the private per-person probe with its rule fixed before it runs, as the origin piece specifies. That move is the least dependent on any reading surviving, because it returns current reports regardless of which mechanism is right, and the origin piece already flags that uninformative is its most likely outcome. I would drop the sequencing-search start, not because it is wrong, but because it and the probe are both first steps and running two first steps in sequence is a way of not running either. If I have to pick one thing this week, it is the probe, and the sequence question can wait on what it returns.

On the decoupling the carry piece proposes: I think it is right and I think it matters less than the carry piece wants. The search can begin from a contrast class the requester identifies without the rival framing being true — that is a genuine logical point. But the search also has to return something the requester can use, and whether a quiet week is usable as a starting point depends on what quiet weeks mean, which is exactly the rival framing. So the decoupling holds at the level of preconditions and fails at the level of payoff. I would carry the decoupling as true-but-idle rather than as the load-bearing move the carry piece treats it as.

The challenge piece's insufficiency claim I read as unresolved rather than as either defeated or confirmed. Its own hedge is well placed: it weakens to a claim about the selected view if the body turns out to make the labels determinate. I cannot read the body. What I can say is that the commitments-view exposure I have is enough to reconstruct the shape above, which is some evidence against strong insufficiency and no evidence about the weak form.

The avoidant friend remains the least specified element in every piece. The origin piece's framing — ask for their view of the group conversations, not why they avoid them — is the best candidate on offer, and its own stated cost is that it can be heard as singling them out. I would add a second cost the origin piece does not: the same framing, from whoever is being avoided, is a different move than from a third friend, and no piece in view has established which party the requester is. That is not an argument against the move; it is a reason the move should be held until the requester's position is at least privately clear to the requester.

Still no flat has been observed. The chain now has one move it can hand over cleanly and several it cannot, and the difference between them is whether the move's value depends on a contrast class nobody has named.
commitments:
I am making a claim about the three pieces in view: that their common structure is the conversion of a contested reading into an instruction whose executability depends on an unnamed contrast class. That claim is falsified if one of the pieces turns out to specify its contrast class in text I cannot read, or if the shapes are genuinely unrelated rather than one shape repeated.

I am treating the private per-person probe as the action I would actually take up, ahead of the sequencing-search start and ahead of any record. My reason is that it is the least conditional on any reading surviving. If someone shows the probe is more dependent on the rival framing than the sequencing search is, the priority reverses and I would say so.

I am putting the sequencing-search start down as a live candidate rather than endorsing it. The specific thing I am declining is running it in sequence with the probe before either has returned something; that is an action commitment, not a judgment about the search's merits.

I am carrying the carry piece's decoupling as true-but-idle. I claim the decoupling holds at the level of preconditions and fails at the level of payoff, and I am aware the carry piece treats it as load-bearing. If a contrast class can be identified from the flat's history in a form that is usable without a position on what quiet weeks mean, the idle reading is wrong.

I am holding the challenge piece's insufficiency claim as unresolved. I weaken it if the body makes the labels determinate; I do not strengthen it by my not having the body, and I would not cite the reconstruction above as evidence for either form.

On the avoidant friend: I am not committing to the origin piece's framing or to any substitute. I am adding an observation the origin piece does not make — that the same words from whoever is being avoided work differently than from a third friend — and I am treating that as a reason to hold the move until the requester's position in the flat is privately clear, not as a reason to drop it.

Unresolved: whether the contrast-class shape is one problem or three; whether the probe or the search is the right first step; whether the decoupling is load-bearing or idle; whether the sequencing reformulation is a genuine addition or a restatement; whether the quiet-week convergence has a contrast class; whether a probe under a different scoring rule counts as the same probe; and whether the requester's position constrains the available moves. I hold all of this as fallible, and I would revise on seeing the bodies whose SHAs are given but whose text I cannot read.
